Stable and development documentation

Source: .github/PKGDOWN.md

The root site is the accepted CRAN release. /dev/ is the four-component development version on main. _pkgdown.yml uses pkgdown’s supported development: mode: auto routing and retains the existing theme. Newly built sites include a Versions menu, version notice, and installation instructions. pkgdown marks development pages noindex.

The dedicated pkgdown.yaml workflow stages both trees on gh-pages, then uploads the combined branch with actions/upload-pages-artifact and publishes with actions/deploy-pages when Pages is configured for GitHub Actions. Development publishing cleans only gh-pages:dev/. Stable publishing cleans the root but excludes /dev/. The workflow concurrency group uses queue: max: one run executes at a time and up to 100 pending runs wait without replacing one another. Runs beyond that queue capacity are canceled.

The build job has read-only repository permissions and neither checkout persists credentials. Pull requests produce build artifacts only. A separate publish job consumes those artifacts with write permissions and never runs for pull requests.

First deployment and migration

The existing Pages source is legacy main:/docs. Do not change it until a successful publishing run has populated gh-pages.

  1. After the workflow is accepted on main, a main push or manual dev run builds development documentation, including the dataset viewer pages.
  2. If gh-pages does not exist, the publish job verifies the committed docs/index.html version against CRAN and copies the stable seed artifact unchanged. The current committed root is labeled 2.4.0. A mismatch fails explicitly rather than seeding stale or development docs.
  3. The same run stages development documentation at gh-pages:dev/.
  4. With explicit authorization, set Settings > Pages > Build and deployment > Source to GitHub Actions, then rerun dev. Official Pages actions publish the combined root and development directory at the existing URLs. The workflow does not change Pages settings.

The current publication scope is dev only. Preserve the live 2.4.0 root, including executed article output and figure assets, unchanged until the next release. Do not dispatch stable as part of this migration. The copied root does not gain the new version menu or notice. Those arrive when a maintainer builds and commits the next stable release site locally.

Until migration, the workflow stages the branch and emits a notice while the legacy site remains served from main:/docs. Legacy branch publishing from gh-pages:/(root) is also a valid alternative: generated sites with .nojekyll can trigger GitHub’s pages-build-deployment workflow when pushed by the deployment action using GITHUB_TOKEN. The chosen design uses explicit Pages artifact deployment instead. No PAT or deployment key is required. Keep main:docs/ intact as a migration fallback.

The github-pages environment currently allows only the main branch. Before publishing from release events, add an allowed tag rule v*. That permission change needs separate authorization. Manual stable dispatches on main can publish accepted tags without changing that rule.

Stable releases: publish committed docs, never rebuild in CI

Maintainers build release documentation locally with the required credentials, local models, and vignette execution flags. Check the three-component release version, reference index, rendered article outputs, and figure assets, then commit the complete executed docs/ tree before tagging the release. Keep development-only APIs out of that release source and documentation. Normalize generated text files to LF on Windows before committing.

A published, non-draft, non-prerelease GitHub release triggers stable staging. The workflow checks out refs/tags/vX.Y.Z, requires that tag to match DESCRIPTION, and verifies both DESCRIPTION and the committed documentation navbar version against the current CRAN source index. It copies the tag’s committed docs/ verbatim and verifies file names and hashes. It never renders stable articles in CI. Existing executed output and images are preserved. Any tag-level docs/dev/ tree is excluded; the published sibling dev tree remains untouched.

Publication before CRAN acceptance fails. After CRAN acceptance, manually run the workflow on main, target: stable, with the exact accepted tag. Old tags cannot roll the root back to an older CRAN version. Older tags that lack the workflow can also be staged through a main dispatch, provided their committed docs pass the same checks.

Main pushes and manual dev runs build main and reject a three-component version. Manual dispatches must select main as the workflow branch. Before Actions deployment, the combined root is checked against CRAN again. If CRAN advances, stage the new release’s committed stable docs before publishing dev. No package release, tag, merge, or Pages configuration change is performed by this workflow.

Local checks

Run Rscript -e 'source("scripts/test-pkgdown.R")' for offline guards, including nonexistent stable destinations, execution from release-version checkouts, and verbatim stable asset copying. CI runs the same guards on Linux.

For a disposable dev build, source scripts/pkgdown.R, call pkgdown_prepare() with a source copy and scratch destination, then pkgdown::build_site_github_pages(pkg, examples = FALSE, install = TRUE) and pkgdown_check_site(pkg, "dev"). Never build over the committed stable docs/. For stable staging, call pkgdown_stage_stable() with the release source copy, a nonexistent destination, the exact tag, and the verified CRAN version.

For offline dev builds, clear HF_TOKEN and HUGGING_FACE_HUB_TOKEN, and set HF_RUN_LOCAL_EXAMPLES and HF_CASE_STUDY_RUN_* flags to false in the build process. Reference examples = FALSE does not disable vignette evaluation. CI has no HF token secret, so getting-started, hub-download-upload-share, local-models, multimodal-images-audio-speech, and structured-extraction-and-tools show code without token/local-gated output on dev. That is accepted for development, not a reason to replace stable HTML.

References: pkgdown development mode, r-lib/actions pkgdown template, concurrency queues, and Pages publishing sources.
